recent_works.title: The Teapot pours – launch of Transport Phenomena and Open Transport : inaugural editorial
recent_works.abstract: Abstract The launch of Transport Phenomena and Open Transport marks the inauguration of two sibling journals with a shared scientific scope dedicated to advancing the science of flow, heat, and diffusion. While Transport Phenomena is offered as a classic library subscription journal with its hybrid open-access option, Open Transport is fully open access. Together, they give authors the freedom to choose their preferred publishing format without relinquishing their preferred editorships or compromising editorial standards. Our mission is to advance excellence in the transport sciences while fostering a supportive and inclusive scholarly environment. Guided by the core principles of excellence, ethics, and editorial independence, we are committed to treating authors as we ourselves would wish to be treated – with fairness, alacrity, rigour, and respect. Our partnership with De Gruyter Brill, whose long tradition of academic publishing aligns closely with these values, provides a strong foundation for developing these journals into leading platforms that serve, connect, and advance the global transport sciences community through shared knowledge.

recent_works.title: Advances in computation of Mittag-Leffler function, its inverses and derivatives
recent_works.abstract: Abstract Fractional calculus relies heavily on the Mittag-Leffler function (MLF). In rheology, for instance, fractional differentiation leads immediately to the shear relaxation function in terms of the Mittag-Leffler function of a scalar. However, the Mittag-Leffler function incorporates the gamma function of the dimensionless complex variable z and the dimensionless real parameters α and β . This gamma function limits Mittag-Leffler function implementation in science and engineering. IEEE-754 double precision arithmetic causes overflow problems, particularly for large z $\left\vert z\right\vert $ . In rheology, for instance, large z $\left\vert z\right\vert $ corresponds to long dimensionless relaxations. The use of fractional calculus in increasingly complicated engineering contexts is limited by such difficulties, such as those requiring MLF differentiation or inversion. This work analyzes these problems and explores ways to estimate the MLF using existing computer routines in MATLAB, Fortran, R, Python, and Stata/Mata. The purpose of this work is to review methods to evaluate the Mittag-Leffler function.

recent_works.title: Constrained recoil after cessation of steady shearing flow from polymer rotarance theory
recent_works.abstract: Abstract Herein, we add another canonical rheological material function to our recent series of these derived from rotarance theory. By rotarance , we mean the hydrodynamic resistance to rotation felt by macromolecules in suspension. We thus use the physics of macromolecular orientation, and only this physics, to derive analytical expressions for (i) the ultimate shear recovery and (ii) both normal stress difference responses, in constrained recoil following cessation of steady shearing flow (called simply creep recovery ). By constrained , we mean that both the shear stress is released suddenly, and thereafter, the fluid remains confined between sliding plates with constant gap. The recoil phenomenon in polymeric liquids returns the fluid towards (but never completely to) its initial state. We call the final state, this ultimate shear strain, the ultimate shear recovery . Whereas recoil is absent in Newtonian fluids, it presents in elastic liquids. As with all known results from rotarance theory, we find creep recovery depends on macromolecular structure, and specifically, on the ratio of macromolecular moments of inertia, I 3 / I 1 .
